subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by a shared reply-session-init recovery/serialization policy, or by adding conflict retry/coalescing behavior to each inbound surface that can receive this error?
rationale: Both fix shapes are plausible, but the comments and repository policy point toward a central owner-boundary fix while the exact recovery semantics affect session state and message delivery.

options.title: Shared Session-Init Recovery
options.body: Make the central initializer wait, retry, self-heal, or coalesce conflicts so Slack, WebChat, heartbeat, Signal, Discord, WhatsApp, and future channels inherit the same behavior.

options.title: Surface Retry Parity
options.body: Keep the central conflict behavior and add bounded retry or spooling to every inbound surface that can drop a conflicted event.

options.title: Request Current Live Proof
options.body: Ask for a current-main WebChat or heartbeat reproduction before choosing the permanent owner boundary.

recommendation.title: Shared Session-Init Recovery
recommendation.body: Make the central initializer wait, retry, self-heal, or coalesce conflicts so Slack, WebChat, heartbeat, Signal, Discord, WhatsApp, and future channels inherit the same behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has the strongest recent history on the guarded initializer and accessor boundary where this decision belongs.
